summary: Iter 34 backend batch tested end-to-end via public EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL. All 23 tests PASSED (100%). Verified: (1) POST /api/nutrition/water returns {date, water_ml, goal_met, water_streak, new_badge}; clamps ml to 0..20000; goal_met flips correctly when ml>=water_goal; streak >=1 after first-time same-day goal-met; new_badge is null|'3'|'7'. (2) GET /api/nutrition/today now includes water_ml and water_streak. (3) GET/POST /api/nutrition/goals includes water_goal (default 3000) and POST preserves existing water_goal when the field is omitted. (4) POST /api/heart-rate/log accepts current_bpm (with/without other fields) and GET /api/heart-rate/today returns current_bpm. Empty body -> 400. (5) GET /api/founders returns 200, includes the owner-admin (previously excluded), does not crash on hardened level_from_xp; GET /api/profile/me idempotently adds 'founder' badge for is_founder users. (6) GET /api/founders/spots public, includes admin in taken count. (7) POST /api/admin/members/{uid}/delete: 403 for non-admin (bot1), 400 for self-delete, 400 for admin target, 404 for unknown; admin path successfully deleted a throwaway QA account (email TEST_iter34_*@qa-example.com), invalidated its session, and a second delete returned 404. (8) GET /api/gyms/nearby returns proper shape and cached:true on 2nd identical call; auth required.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/nutrition.py POST /nutrition/water: when goal was already met earlier today (sdate == d), the returned water_streak comes from the in-memory user object loaded at request start, which is fine here, but note the endpoint never re-reads the user after the $addToSet/$set updates for the badge case — the response 'water_streak' still reflects the new value because it's computed locally. No functional bug, but consider re-fetching to keep response and DB truly in lock-step.

routes/nutrition.py nutrition_today: streak reset happens client-side only (line 16-17), not persisted. If a user skips >1 day the DB still shows the stale streak; only next goal-met write correctly resets. Cosmetic — /today response is correct.

routes/admin.py admin_delete_member: order of guards puts self-check AFTER is_admin-check, so an admin trying to delete themselves returns 400 with 'Cannot delete an admin account' (not 'You cannot delete your own account'). Message-order mismatch only; both are 400. Consider swapping the two checks so self-delete surfaces the correct message.
routes/profile.py gyms_nearby: cache_key includes radius, but the request-batch spec says 'per rounded coord'. Passing a different radius bypasses cache — acceptable but worth documenting.
seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up a throwaway registered member (TEST_iter34_<hex>@qa-example.com, display TEST_Iter34Del) purely to exercise admin delete. Deleted at end of test. No bot / owner / real accounts touched.
